brief.topic: Measuring an agent only by whether the final answer was right
brief.audience: PMs and engineers evaluating AI agents

coreInsight: A correct final answer can hide wrong tool calls, wasted steps and risky actions, so evaluate an agent’s trajectory — tools, steps and unapproved actions — not just its output.

scenes.onScreen: GRADE THE TRAJECTORY / Check the path, not just the end. / CHECK → LOOK FOR → FAIL IF / Tool choice → Right tool, right args → Wrong or made-up tool · Steps taken → Close to expected → Loops or detours · Risky actions → Approved first → Any unapproved write / Log every step, not just the output · Review failed paths, even on passes

caption.opening: An agent can reach the right answer the wrong way, and a final-answer eval will score it a pass.
body:
What a final-answer check misses:
→ the wrong tool, or made-up arguments, that happened to work
→ fourteen steps for a three-step job (cost and latency)
→ an action nobody approved, like sending an email

Grade the trajectory too:
→ tool choice and arguments
→ step count against what you expect
→ any write or external action without approval = fail
(The three runs in the reel are illustrative examples.)

claims.text: Evaluating agents only on the final answer misses wrong tool use, wasted steps and unapproved actions; trajectories should be evaluated as well.
Three example runs, including one taking 14 steps for a 3-step job.
